# Checklist: security
<!-- Generated by /speckit.checklist -->
<!-- Branch: 004-contas-avatar | Date: 2026-09-09 -->

The first feature to accept **credentials** and hold **personal data**, some of it from students.
Constitution Principle 5 makes security review mandatory here, and this is part of it — run
**before** implementation, unlike 003's.

Adjudicated against spec, plan and task list. Every `[ ]` carries an **OPEN** rationale.

| ID | Check | Dimension | FR/US Ref | Status |
|----|-------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| CHK039 | Is the password never stored, transmitted or logged in a recoverable form?<br>**Adjudicated:** Payload hashes; FR-020 forbids logging and T017 scans emitted lines rather than reading code. | [data-protection] | FR-020, SC-005 | [x] |
| CHK040 | Does a failed login reveal which half failed, or whether the address exists?<br>**Adjudicated:** no — FR-014 and SC-002 require byte-identical body and status, which is already Payload's behaviour and is asserted rather than assumed. | [authentication] | FR-014, SC-002 | [x] |
| CHK041 | Does password reset reveal whether an address is registered?<br>**Adjudicated:** not in body or status. **Timing does** — the registered branch writes and sends mail while the other returns. Recorded in SC-003 as accepted, not overlooked. | [authentication] | FR-017, SC-003 | [x] |
| CHK042 | Is login rate-limited in a way an attacker cannot sidestep?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN** — see CHK014. Payload limits **per account**; FR-015 also asks per source, and nothing implements it. An attacker spraying one password across many accounts is unaffected by a per-account lock. | [authentication] | FR-015, SC-004 | [ ] |
| CHK043 | Is the session invalidated server-side on sign-out, not merely cleared client-side?<br>**Adjudicated:** FR-018 requires it and T013b now distinguishes the two — it had no task before this pass. | [authentication] | FR-018 | [x] |
| CHK044 | Is the account-creation path itself abusable — can a stranger create accounts in bulk?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN.** Phase 1 has no verification (CLR-006), no CAPTCHA and no signup rate limit, so bulk creation is possible. What it buys is bounded — 002's `canPublishField` means drafts, never published content — but the moderation queue is the target and nothing in 004 defends it. | [input-sanitization] | FR-019, CLR-006 | [ ] |
| CHK045 | Does an unverified account reach anything a verified one would not?<br>**Adjudicated:** phase 1 has no such distinction, by decision. Recorded so a later reader does not assume a gate exists. | [authorization] | CLR-006 | [x] |
| CHK046 | Is the signed-in read path distinguished from the anonymous one, so a signed-in page cannot borrow `overrideAccess`?<br>**Adjudicated:** FR-028 names `getTenantScopedPayload(req)`; the plan states the anonymous path is neither used nor widened; T038 tests it. | [authorization] | FR-028, US10 | [x] |
| CHK047 | Can a maker of one lab read or write another lab's profile, skills or content?<br>**Adjudicated:** SC-007 forbids it and T038 drives the signed-in vantage point across every page this feature adds. | [authorization] | FR-029, SC-007, US10 | [x] |
| CHK048 | Has the **write-side** guard ever been proved able to fail?<br>**Adjudicated:** not before this feature — no mutation layer covered `sameTenant`. T036 adds one and must be watched red before T037 wires the CI job. | [authorization] | FR-029, SC-008 | [x] |
| CHK049 | Is the handle collision resolved somewhere a race cannot defeat?<br>**Adjudicated:** a unique index plus retry; the database adjudicates. T021 drives two concurrent creates, because a race only reproducible under load is the one nobody reproduces. | [data-protection] | FR-010, SC-009 | [x] |
| CHK050 | Is personal data enumerable through any identifier this feature exposes?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN.** `@handle` is derived from a real name and is public on every card, so the handle set is a directory of the lab's members — inherent to the design and accepted. What is **not** examined is whether profile ids leak elsewhere; 003's CHK071 raised the same question for content ids and left it open. | [data-protection] | FR-010 | [ ] |
| CHK051 | Does deletion actually erase, or only hide?<br>**Adjudicated:** CLR-003 erases the personal data, keeps the work under a tombstone, and removes the person's likes. SC-010 asserts all three. | [data-protection] | FR-031, SC-010, US8 | [x] |
| CHK052 | Is the legal basis for holding each field recorded?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN** — see CHK027. FR-030 requires the record and T040 produces it, but the basis itself is ISS-002's, pending UNESP review. | [data-protection] | FR-030 | [ ] |
| CHK053 | Is consent recorded in a form that survives a change to the terms?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — the **version** as well as the timestamp (FR-012, SC-013), so a re-consent can be demanded and the two populations distinguished. | [data-protection] | FR-012, SC-013 | [x] |
| CHK054 | Is the avatar upload treated as hostile input?<br>**Adjudicated:** it goes through 002's media collections and their limits (FR-033, T035b) rather than a second path — and 002 already checks magic bytes and generates the object key rather than trusting a filename. | [input-sanitization] | FR-033 | [x] |
